children: U.S. Treasury yields moved modestly lower Friday morning after the latest consumer price index report showed August inflation coming in largely as expected.
rose 0.4% month over month, matching forecasts. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3%, a slight tick above the 0.2% consensus.
slipped 5 basis points to 5.31% after touching an earlier high of 5.42%. At the same time, the U.S. 10 Year Treasury yield
fell 4 basis points to 4.92% after nearly tagging 5%, with an intraday peak of 4.99%. The U.S. 2 Year Treasury yield
edged 1 basis point higher to 4.59% after reaching 4.65% earlier in the session.

The mixed but mostly softer long-end reaction reflects a market that viewed the headline print as confirmatory rather than a fresh inflation surprise, even as the core reading ran a bit hotter than expected. Yields had pushed higher into the data before easing once the numbers were absorbed.

The report leaves the inflation path intact without a clear catalyst for a sharp repricing of the policy outlook. Traders will continue to watch upcoming labor and spending data for the next directional cue.

title: Treasury yields ease as markets digest August CPI data
